scope: Initial source, attribution, date, context, and x-risk judgment spot checks. Each case checks one statement, not every statement on the profile.

sampling.congress: Six current profiles: three sampled from score >=3 and three from nonzero scores below 3; inspect a cited non-X statement.
sampling.executive: Eight purposive profiles spanning high, low, unscored, and truncated evidence.
limitations: No population accuracy estimate is valid from this sample.
A source match verifies quotation presence, not the truth of the speaker's claim.
Current-role eligibility was not rechecked in this source audit.
This sample does not validate all five dimensions, the 23 regulation categories, summaries, or named-policy judgments.
Original pipeline judgments remain in place pending independent review. Astra overall-stance reviews do not validate x-risk labels.

cases.name: John Kennedy
cases.finding: The syndicated USA TODAY article attributes the quotation to Kennedy. His nearby remarks connect the shutoff proposal to loss of human control. That context supports level 3. The original URL was unavailable.
cases.reviewer: Codex source audit; not a blinded second judge

cases.name: George Whitesides
cases.finding: The source matches the quotation and attributes the op-ed to Whitesides. The surrounding text explicitly discusses existential risk and recursive self-improvement. Judge B omitted an x-risk label; review the quotation with this context.
cases.reviewer: Codex source audit; not a blinded second judge

cases.name: Brad Sherman
cases.finding: The mirror attributes the speech to Sherman. The nearby text discusses extinction and loss of control. The statement ranks his control-system legislation as his most important legislation, supporting level 4. This check did not recover an office-hosted original.
cases.reviewer: Codex source audit; not a blinded second judge

cases.name: Tim Kaine
cases.finding: The syndicated WVNS story supports both quoted segments and their attribution to Kaine. The stored ellipsis marks their join. The article does not establish a specific catastrophic scenario. Review x-risk relevance and the date; an earlier September 17 broadcast transcript contains similar remarks.
cases.reviewer: Codex source audit; not a blinded second judge

cases.name: Jamie Raskin
cases.finding: The source attributes the quotation to Raskin and dates the event to September 30. The stored date was missing. A human-species security concern supports a risk label; this excerpt does not specify a response to catastrophic risk.
cases.reviewer: Codex source audit; not a blinded second judge

cases.name: Zachary Nunn
cases.finding: The source attributes both passages to Nunn. The stored quotation joins them across reporter attribution and changes the boundary punctuation. It is a composite quotation, not one contiguous match. The article dates the event to Thursday, October 15; the stored date used the October 16 publication date. Level 2 is defensible for the excerpt; nearby reporting describes a commission proposal.
cases.reviewer: Codex source audit; not a blinded second judge
cases.correction: date corrected; composite quote marked with an ellipsis

cases.name: Helena Fu
cases.finding: The signed testimony attributes the passage to Fu. It describes evaluations and red teaming for chemical, biological, radiological and nuclear misuse. The shared rubric includes this class of catastrophic misuse and its response.
cases.reviewer: Codex source audit; not a blinded second judge

cases.name: Paul Christiano
cases.finding: The exact excerpt warns about permanent loss of control. The following passage calls for coordination, mitigation, and slower development when necessary. Review the excerpt boundary before resolving the current level 3 versus level 2 disagreement. The page verifies authorship, not current government eligibility.
cases.reviewer: Codex source audit; not a blinded second judge

cases.name: Michael Kratsios
cases.finding: The exact quotation concerns speculative risks and regulatory costs. Its nearby context covers tyranny, adoption, trust, and regulation, without an explicit catastrophic scenario. Review the DeepSeek x-risk label of 1; Sol supplied no x-risk label. Another statement on this profile explicitly rejects existential-risk concerns, so this case does not establish that the whole profile should be unscored.
cases.reviewer: Codex source audit; not a blinded second judge

cases.name: JD Vance
cases.finding: The stored X excerpt starts with the end of a prior sentence and ends before the example. The full post immediately gives consumer fraud as that example. The rubric excludes scams from catastrophic risk. Review the DeepSeek x-risk label of 1; Sol supplied no x-risk label. Direct page retrieval matched the fragment and account name; this audit did not repeat official API identity verification.
cases.reviewer: Codex source audit; not a blinded second judge

cases.name: Donald Trump
cases.finding: The official transcript identifies the President as the speaker. The surrounding exchange concerns AI competition with China. It supports the China dimension, without an explicit catastrophic scenario. No x-risk label is appropriate for this excerpt.
cases.reviewer: Codex source audit; not a blinded second judge

cases.name: Ethan Klein
cases.finding: The opening statement identifies Klein and the hearing date. The passage concerns an international AI race, without an explicit catastrophic scenario. No x-risk label is appropriate for this excerpt.
cases.reviewer: Codex source audit; not a blinded second judge

cases.name: Russell Vought
cases.finding: The cited third-party draft PDF was unavailable. A later signed final memorandum contains related language, but it is a different document version. This audit cannot verify the original draft quotation or its date. The collection follow-up adds separate verified passages from signed official memoranda.
cases.reviewer: Codex source audit; not a blinded second judge

cases.name: Timothy Kosiba
cases.finding: The article attributes the quotation to Kosiba at an event on August 27. A request for model access does not, by itself, express a catastrophic-risk stance. No x-risk label is appropriate for this excerpt.
cases.reviewer: Codex source audit; not a blinded second judge
